plan.title: Legacy upgrade deletes .deft/core on a dirty tree without warning (successor to #4158)

narratives.Description: OVPR fix plan unit P2-U6, second brief (story id ovpr-p2-u6b), spec units/P2-U6-upgrade-task-works-and-is-honest.md and drafts/RC-03.md, issues #6002 and #6022. Split from the P2-U6 brief because its file list lacks the new test file and the evaluator-surface disclosure file, and briefs cannot be widened. Part 1 (#6002, RC-03, approved D-030): when upgrade converts an old-layout project, the plan lists the files Git reports as modified or untracked under .deft/core (the first 20, then a count), with no prompt, no refusal and no exit-code change. Part 2 (#6022 cleanup): the root Taskfile.yml `upgrade` and `uninstall` alias descriptions say the task is retired and name the `directive` command, and the stale comment naming `install-upgrade` is removed.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary
`directive upgrade` from the legacy layout deletes `.deft/core` on a dirty tree without any warning. Uncommitted local edits there are lost, and git can't bring them back. #4158 (closed) covered "refuse dirty consumer upgrades before writes" for the old `deft update`.

## Steps / Actual
0.126.2 deposit with 149 uncommitted paths (the whole fresh deposit). The commit was blocked by the old hooks once the global launcher was 0.127 (see #5960). `directive upgrade --yes` → plan says "remove the copied .deft/core tree (including any local edits there)", with no mention of uncommitted changes, and proceeds. Exit 0.

## Expected
Warn (or require explicit approval) when the tree is dirty, especially for the paths about to be deleted. In non-interactive mode with `--yes`, at minimum list the uncommitted paths that will be removed.

## Root cause
- Cause: the OVPR upgrade plan presents a generic removal note and does not inspect git status before deleting the legacy tree.
- Evidence: upgrade plan and output (upgrade log); #4158 precedent.
- Confidence: likely (behavior confirmed; plan code not read).
- Checked: upgrade on a dirty tree.

Refs #4158

## Environment
- Directive 0.127.0 (`@deftai/directive` launcher + `@deftai/directive-runtime`), `latest` dist-tag
- Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, Node 24.20.0, npm 11.19.0, pnpm 10.33.2, Git for Windows (system gitconfig `core.autocrlf=true`)
- Shells: Git Bash, PowerShell 7, cmd.exe. Isolated npm prefix/cache; registry = local Verdaccio proxying npmjs. Throwaway fixture repos.
narratives.StoryId: ovpr-p2-u6b (carried in the file name so the ordered plan can match it; plan.id stays the id minted from the issue, because the brief tools refuse a different plan.id)
narratives.UnitSpec: ~/Projects/directive-ovpr-planning-202611/units/P2-U6-upgrade-task-works-and-is-honest.md and ~/Projects/directive-ovpr-planning-202611/drafts/RC-03.md (read both in full; an 'Update 2026-11-17' banner wins over the text below it).
narratives.ImplementationPlan: Part 1 (#6002): the upgrade bookend (packages/cli/src/bookends.ts) runs `git status --porcelain -- .deft/core` read-only before the plan is shown, only for old-layout conversion. packages/cli/src/plan-present.ts lists the reported paths under the existing removal line (the first 20, then a count of the rest), in both the human and the keyed plan output. Not a Git repo, Git missing, or nothing reported: no list, plan unchanged. Test in packages/cli/src/upgrade-deft-core-edits.test.ts; fragment changelog.d/6002-upgrade-lists-deft-core-edits.md. Part 2 (#6022): in the root Taskfile.yml, change the `upgrade` and `uninstall` alias `desc` lines to say the task is retired and name `directive upgrade` / `directive uninstall`; delete the stale comment block above `upgrade` that names `install-upgrade`. Taskfile.yml is an evaluator surface, so add the disclosure record in xbrief/evaluator-surface-disposition.json.
narratives.Constraint:
- #6002: list only. No prompt, no refusal, no exit-code change, no clean-tree requirement; `--yes` still approves the plan (RC-03 option B; AC5.3, AC5.13).
- The Git read is read-only. Do not stash, commit, reset or change anything in the user's Git state.
- Do not merge the #6002 change before RC-03's docs PR (AC10.6 and the requirements section A9 mitigation cell) has merged (D-030).
- Do not make `task upgrade` or `task uninstall` run `directive` (or anything else). Retired names are not redirected (AC13.6).
- Do not add a new verb, flag or upgrade path.
- Do not edit the P2-U6 brief.
- OVPR change gate: read ~/Projects/directive-ovpr-planning-202611/OVPR-CHANGE-GATE.md. Do not edit docs/installer-refactor-ovpr/ and do not ship behaviour that departs from the written OVPR requirements or architecture; stop that part and hand back a change proposal.
- Changelog: add the changelog.d fragment named in file_scope; never edit CHANGELOG.md.
narratives.Dependencies: Depends on P2-U6 (plan.id github.issue.6142058296; its first PR #6661 for #6022 is in the merge queue). The #6002 part also depends on requirements change RC-03 (approved by polfer, D-030): its docs-only PR #6630 must merge before this code merges. Blocks: none.
narratives.PlanningOrder: design-critique: not warranted, because the OVPR fix plan and this unit spec already decide the design (polfer decisions D-001, D-008)
narratives.Traces: Closes #6002 (RC-03 option B). Refs #6022 (Taskfile.yml alias cleanup left over from P2-U6's first PR).
narratives.UserStory: As a person upgrading an old-layout project, I want the upgrade plan to list the edited or new files Git sees under .deft/core before it deletes that folder, and the retired task aliases to name the directive command, so that I can save my files first and know which command to run.

items.title: When upgrade converts an old-layout project, the plan lists the files Git reports as modified or untracked under `.deft/core` (the first 20, then a count of the rest).

narrative.Acceptance: Given an old-layout project where Git reports modified or untracked files under `.deft/core`, when `directive upgrade` shows its conversion plan, then the plan lists those files under the `.deft/core` removal line, the first 20 by path and then a count of the rest.

items.title: The list adds no prompt and no refusal and does not change the exit code; `--yes` still approves the plan and a clean working tree is still not required.

narrative.Acceptance: Given the same project, when `directive upgrade --yes` runs, then it asks no extra question, does not refuse, removes `.deft/core` as before, and exits with the same code as without the list.

items.title: The Git read is read-only, and when Git reports nothing (or the project is not a Git repo) the plan is unchanged.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a project where `.deft/core` is clean, ignored, or not in a Git repo, when the conversion plan is shown, then no file list appears and the plan text is unchanged; and in every case the upgrade does not change the Git index, stash or branches.

items.title: The root `Taskfile.yml` `upgrade` and `uninstall` alias descriptions say the task is retired and name `directive upgrade` / `directive uninstall`, and no comment there names `install-upgrade`.

narrative.Acceptance: Given the root `Taskfile.yml`, when its `upgrade` and `uninstall` aliases are read, then each `desc` says the task is retired and names `directive upgrade` or `directive uninstall`, and the file has no comment naming `install-upgrade`.

issueCommentThread.body:
### Duplicate / uniqueness triage (2026-10-28)

**Verdict: UNIQUE — keep open (explicit OVPR successor of a closed ticket).**

Not a row in the sealed install-ovpr-problem-ledger-2026-10-23 map.

**Related (not duplicate):**
- Closed #4158 / fix #4448 — refuse dirty consumer upgrades before writes for old `deft update`
- Open #5960 — related upgrade friction under mixed layouts (different: stale-CLI write gate / all-repos upgrade pressure)

Do not reopen #4158. Implement the dirty-tree warn/list (or refuse) on `directive upgrade` deleting `.deft/core` under this ticket.
